MUQATIL:90:17-20/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:90:17-20/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:90:17-20/r1.claim: Faith means believing in God, angels, scriptures, messengers, Paradise, and Hell; believers exhort one another to persevere in Quranic duties, without which their charity and expiation are not accepted.

MUQATIL:90:17-20/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:90:17-20/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:90:17-20/r2.claim: Showing mercy means maintaining kinship ties and not severing them.

FARRA:v3p264/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p264/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p264/r1.claim: Arabic usually repeats lā across coordinated statements; here one lā covers the three parts of the steep path: freeing a slave or feeding during famine, then believing.

TUSTARI:90:17/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:90:17/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:90:17/r1.claim: Mutual counsel in patience means patience in obeying God, while mutual mercy means compassion among creatures.

TUSTARI:90:17/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:90:17/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:90:17/r2.claim: Asked about Islam, the Prophet answered patience and generosity; asked about faith, he answered wholesome speech and feeding people.

TUSTARI:90:17/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:90:17/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:90:17/r3.claim: Sahl says the best speech is remembrance of God.

TAB:90:17/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:17/r1.speaker: author
TAB:90:17/r1.claim: The person who boasted of spending abundant wealth must join believers, mutually encourage endurance in God's cause, and urge compassion toward others.

TAB:90:17/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:90:17/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains mutual exhortation to compassion as showing mercy to people.

ZAJJAJ:v5p329#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p329#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p329#2/r4.claim: The person first does these deeds while holding the bond of faith, then remains steadfast in faith; mutual counsel means patience in obedience and away from sin, and compassion.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3435#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3435#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3435#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says mutual compassion means showing mercy to all people.

NAHHAS:v5p232/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p232/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p232/r8.claim: Then they remained steadfast in faith; an alternative takes thumma as sequencing or simply reporting what follows.

NAHHAS:v5p232/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p232/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p232/r9.claim: The repeated verb and preposition in urging patience and compassion add emphasis.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p414/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p414/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p414/r2.claim: Being among the believers is necessary for the freeing and other good deeds to benefit, because disbelief cancels their reward.

THALABI:v10p211/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p211/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p211/r1.claim: Some take thumma as waw; mutual exhortation means that people urge one another to patience and compassion toward others.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r12.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r12.claim: Urging patience means patience in obeying God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r13.speaker: هشام بن حسان
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r13.claim: It may mean patience with what God has made obligatory.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r14.speaker: سفيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r14.claim: It may mean patience in enduring what befalls people.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r15.claim: It may also mean patience in worldly life and resisting its desires.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p279/r16.claim: Urging compassion means showing mercy to one another and to all people; alternatively, it means urging one another toward the afterlife, the abode of mercy, by leaving worldly life behind.

QUSHAYRI:v3p422/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p422/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p422/r16.claim: The outcome depends on ending one's life among the faithful.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r1.claim: The person who surmounts the obstacle by freeing a neck or feeding must also be among the believers; without faith the act of devotion is nullified by disbelief.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r2.claim: Thumma signals sequence in the wording, not sequence in existence: the good deeds were done while the person was a believer.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r3.claim: They explain the phrase as being among the believers along with performing these deeds; a cited poem uses thumma to add a forefather's status without chronological order.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r4.claim: It may also mean that the person ultimately dies a believer, which makes the good deeds beneficial.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r5.claim: Alternatively, someone who did good seeking God before believing in Muhammad can receive its reward after later accepting Islam.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r6.speaker: حكيم بن حزام عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p34/r6.claim: After accepting Islam, Hakim asked whether his good pre-Islamic religious acts counted; the Prophet replied that he had accepted Islam on the basis of the good he had sent ahead.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p36/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p36/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p36/r1.claim: Patience means remaining steadfast in fulfilling God's obligations and commands.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p36/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p36/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p36/r2.claim: Mercy means treating one another compassionately, especially the orphan, the poor, and the weak.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p36/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p36/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p36/r3.claim: These qualities describe companions including Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf.

WAHIDI-QT:90:17/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:90:17/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:90:17/r1.claim: The earlier good deeds benefit only those who are believers; they urge one another to obey God and show compassion toward creation.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:90:14-20/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:90:14-20/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:90:14-20/r4.claim: Freeing a slave and feeding only count as crossing the ascent when the person also believes; believers counsel one another to obey God patiently and show mercy to creation.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p433#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p433#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p433#2/r3.claim: Such acts only benefit along with faith; ثم can mean ‘and,’ and people urge one another to fulfill God’s obligations patiently and show mercy.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760#2/r1.claim: ثم marks faith's higher rank and virtue than freeing slaves and charity, not later timing: faith precedes these acts and is necessary for any good deed to stand.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760#2/r2.claim: المرحمة means mercy: believers may urge one another to remain firm in faith; to avoid sins, perform duties, and endure trials while showing compassion; or to do what brings God's mercy.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p760#2/r6.claim: A report promises safety from God's anger on Judgment Day for whoever recites Surat al-Balad.

TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r10.claim: Believers urge one another to show mercy to the poor and needy, or more broadly to all people.

TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:90:1-20#7/r9.claim: Good works benefit only alongside faith and steadfastness in belief; patience means keeping obligations and avoiding disobedience.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#5/r1.claim: Here thumma functions like wāw: freeing and feeding only benefit when joined with faith.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#5/r2.claim: Mutual exhortation to patience concerns God's obligations and commands; mutual exhortation to mercy means showing compassion to one another.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#5/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#5/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p135#5/r3.claim: The identities of the people of the right and left were explained at al-Wāqiʿa 56:7-8.

RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r1.claim: The one who passed the difficult ascent must also belong to the believers; without faith, none of these acts benefits its doer.

RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r2.claim: The delayed mention of faith may be rhetorical rather than chronological, as in a poem that mentions a father's and grandfather's status after the son's.

RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, faith must be the person's final state at death, since dying in faith is required for reward from earlier obedience.

RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r4.claim: A third view allows reward for good deeds done before conversion if the person later accepts Muhammad; Hakim ibn Hizam asked about his pre-Islamic good works and the Prophet replied that he entered Islam with them.

RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r5.claim: A fourth reading delays faith in rank, not time: its reward greatly exceeds freeing a slave or giving charity.

RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r6.claim: Mutual exhortation to patience means steadfastness in faith, obedience, avoiding sins and enduring trials.

RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r7.claim: Mutual exhortation to mercy means helping the oppressed and poor and restraining a person approaching wrongdoing; it requires directing others toward truth and away from evil.

RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r8.claim: These believers are the leading Companions, including the four caliphs, distinguished by endurance in religion and compassion for people.

RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r9.speaker: بعض المحققين
RAZI-FULL:v31p169#3/r9.claim: A learned authority sums up religious conduct as two foundations: truthfulness toward God and good character toward people.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r1.claim: Freeing a slave or feeding the hungry does not cross the steep path unless accompanied by faith; acceptance of acts requires belief in God.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r2.claim: Faith added only after spending does not help; the Qur'an says disbelief kept hypocrites' spending from acceptance.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r3.speaker: عائشة عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r3.claim: Aisha asks whether Ibn Judʿan's pre-Islamic charity, freeing captives, and hospitality benefit him; the Prophet says no, since he never asked forgiveness for the Day of Judgment.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r4.claim: Alternatively, he did these deeds as a believer and remained faithful until death, like the phrasing in 20:82.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r5.claim: Other interpretations say he believed the deeds would benefit him with God, or performed them for God and then believed in Muhammad.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r6.speaker: حكيم بن حزام عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r6.claim: After Islam, Hakim asked whether his pre-Islamic good deeds counted; the Prophet said he entered Islam with the good he had already done.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r7.claim: Some say thumma means wa: the person who freed or fed was among the believers.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r8.claim: Tawāṣaw means they advised one another to obey God, avoid sins, and endure afflictions, and to show mercy to creation.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب ويحيى بن سلام وابن زيد وميمون بن مهران
QURTUBI-FULL:90:17-19/r9.claim: They explain the people of the right through right-hand records, being fortunate, coming from Adam's right side, or holding a right-side station; the author summarizes them as Paradise's people.

BAYDAWI-FULL:90:17-20/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:17-20/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:17-20/r1.claim: Then is attached to scaling the pass or freeing the captive; faith follows at a higher rank and is prerequisite to other acts of obedience.

BAYDAWI-FULL:90:17-20/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:17-20/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:17-20/r2.claim: They urge one another to patience in obeying God and compassion toward His servants, or acts that bring God’s mercy.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r13.claim: Then being among believers means persisting in faith.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r14.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r14.claim: An alternative takes then in the sense of and.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r15.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r15.claim: Another explanation makes then signal faith's higher rank and virtue, not later timing, since faith precedes other deeds and no good deed stands without it.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r16.claim: Mutual exhortation to patience means avoiding sins, keeping obedient, and enduring the trials believers face.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r17.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#9/r17.claim: Mutual exhortation to compassion means showing mercy to one another.

QASHANI:90:8-14/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:90:8-14/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:90:8-14/r4.claim: Feeding the needy exemplifies generosity and chastity; faith is wisdom, patience is courage that depends on certainty, and compassion is justice, completing the four cardinal virtues.

QASHANI:90:8-14/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:90:8-14/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:90:8-14/r5.claim: The order begins with chastity and generosity, then the higher wisdom of faith, then patience which requires certainty, and ends with compassion as justice; each named quality stands for its broader virtue.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p483/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p483/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p483/r1.claim: The clause about becoming one of the believers is coordinated with the failure to climb; thumma marks rank or order of mention, not time, since belief must precede good deeds and persist until death for them to benefit.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p483/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p483/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p483/r2.claim: Mutual exhortation to patience means steadfastness in faith and obedience and abstention from sins; exhortation to mercy means compassion or acts that bring God's mercy.

SAMIN-DURR:90:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:17/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:90:17/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes ‘thumma’ as a delay in rank and virtue, not time: faith precedes all deeds and is their necessary basis.

SAMIN-DURR:90:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:90:17/r2.claim: Another interpretation means that a person ultimately meets death in faith, a condition for benefiting from acts of devotion.

SAMIN-DURR:90:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:90:17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:90:17/r3.claim: A third explanation makes ‘thumma’ signal delay in the presentation of the ideas.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r1.claim: Alongside the noble traits just described, a person must believe inwardly and hope for God's reward, as in other verses.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r2.claim: Believers urge one another to endure people's harms and to show them mercy.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r3.claim: The Prophet teaches that the Merciful shows mercy to those who show mercy on earth, and calls for mercy to all on earth.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r4.claim: Another Prophetic saying states that God does not show mercy to people who do not show mercy to others.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p408#2/r5.claim: The Prophet says that one who does not show mercy to the young and recognize the right of the old is not of the community.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p433/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p433/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p433/r1.claim: The preceding good deeds signal noble character and high aspiration, and sincerity is required for such qualities; thumma introduces a second, later obstacle concerning purified reason.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p433/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p433/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p433/r2.claim: True believers accepted the caller despite becoming followers after once being followed, reasoning that faith raised them from lowliness toward an exalted rank.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p433/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p433/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p433/r3.claim: The passage’s phrase about people of understanding is linked to the cited signs for those endowed with understanding.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r1.claim: Abu Bakr’s pre-Islamic character included kinship, hospitality, carrying burdens, and helping people facing true calamities; Ibn al-Daghina said such a man should neither leave nor be expelled.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r10.claim: The faithful cultivate mercy through love and aversion for God; faith purifies them from ostentation and self-admiration, making them radiant in knowledge.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r2.claim: Khadija praised similar virtues in the Prophet after his first encounter with Gabriel, paralleling Abu Bakr’s innate virtues.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r3.claim: God enabled Abu Bakr to accept the call to Islam immediately and without hesitation.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r4.claim: At Hudaybiyya Abu Bakr answered Umar with the Prophet’s exact words despite not hearing them beforehand, evidence of his exceptional rank.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r5.claim: Abu Bakr never drank wine; when challenged in pagan times, he said he would spend all his wealth on anything that increased his intelligence.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r6.claim: The Prophet said, ‘I entered Islam carrying forward the good I had done’; this validates Abu Bakr’s good deeds from before Islam through his later faith.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r7.claim: Faith elevates a person and leads to religious duties that require the greater struggle against one’s nature; courage is a third virtue, and its hardship is sustained by patience and cooperation.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r8.claim: The believers mutually counsel patience in demanding acts of duty, including enjoining right even when it may lead to death; bravery is patience for an hour.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p434/r9.claim: Mercy is a fourth obstacle and fruit of patient justice, moderating excess and deficiency; repeating the verb signals that few people practice it, in forms fitting each time and place.

DURR-FULL:v8p525/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p525/r11.speaker: هشام بن حسان
DURR-FULL:v8p525/r11.claim: He explained mutual exhortation to patience as patience in carrying out what God made obligatory.

DURR-FULL:v8p525/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p525/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p525/r12.claim: He said mutual exhortation to mercy means showing mercy to all people.

BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r1.claim: Then marks faith's higher rank after emancipation and charity, although faith comes first in time and is required for every righteous deed; accepted spending is for God, unlike wealth squandered in ostentation and pride.

BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r2.speaker: المحاسبي
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r2.claim: The afterlife's obstacle can be crossed only by one who keeps his stomach from forbidden and doubtful food and takes only enough to preserve life.

BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r3.speaker: القاسم
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r3.claim: Al-Qasim says the obstacle is the self: free it from servitude to creatures and occupy it in worship of the Lord.

BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r4.claim: Mutual counsel in patience means supporting one another in obedience, abstaining from sins, and enduring afflictions.

BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r5.claim: Mutual counsel in mercy means compassion toward God's creatures or encouraging acts that bring His mercy; it is broader than pity for deserving people such as orphans and the poor.

BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r6.claim: The Prophet says God shows no mercy to one who does not show mercy to people.

BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r7.claim: Patience signifies reverence for God's command, while mercy signifies compassion for His creation; mutual counsel perfects others after each person has attained faith and good works.

BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p339#2/r8.claim: A cited teacher calls feeding in severe need the greatest form of self-restraint, faith the highest wisdom, patience a great form of courage, and mutual compassion among the best forms of justice; patience follows faith because courage requires certainty.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r1.claim: Thumma kāna is coordinated with the negative “did not cross”: he neither crossed the ascent nor believed; repeating the negative is rhetorically allowed to single out faith as the noblest part, not because faith lies outside the ascent's sense.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r2.speaker: ابن زيد والجبائي وأبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r2.claim: An alternative reads lā as a prayer against him, or as a shortened lā used for urging (“why did he not cross?”), or supplies a deleted interrogative; Alusi raises grammatical objections to these alternatives.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r3.speaker: الطيبي عن أبي علي الفارسي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r3.claim: Al-Tibi transmits Abu Ali al-Farisi's view that the negative need not be repeated, answering al-Zajjaj; examples such as “they did not spend extravagantly nor stint” show non-repetition.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r4.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p138#4/r4.claim: The grammarians criticize Umar ibn Abi Rabiʿa's line, quoted as an example in the discussion over omitting an interrogative hamza.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r4.claim: The rank conveyed by thumma places faith above the other deeds because it is what secures salvation; faith without later required deeds still saves, whereas deeds without faith do not count.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r5.claim: Mutual counsel in patience can mean steadfastness in faith, obedience, avoiding sin, or enduring trials; mutual counsel in compassion means mercy to God's creatures, including enjoining right, or acts that bring God's mercy.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139/r6.claim: Counsel in patience honors God's command and counsel in compassion shows kindness to creation; these are the two foundations of obedience, expressed by the Sufi maxim to be truthful with God and good in character with people.

ELMALILI:90:12-20/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r14.claim: Because “then he was” is coordinated with “he undertook,” the sense is negative: he neither attempted the ascent nor became one of the believers.

ELMALILI:90:12-20/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:12-20/r15.claim: Believers also encourage one another to patience and mercy, giving consolation and strength even when they cannot perform the demanding acts of freeing and feeding.

QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r1.claim: Here “then” marks spiritual rank and breadth, not chronological order: faith must precede emancipation and feeding, and gives righteous action weight by connecting it to a stable divine way rather than whim, praise, or advantage.

QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r2.claim: Patience is essential to faith and especially to confronting the obstacle; mutual exhortation exceeds individual patience by strengthening communal endurance and preventing discouragement, defeat, and panic.

QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r3.claim: Mutual exhortation to compassion adds a shared and collective duty of mercy to mercy itself, with everyone recognizing and supporting that obligation.

QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:90:17/r4.claim: The passage stresses Islam as a communal religion and the Qur’an and Prophetic teachings repeatedly underscore that community, while retaining clear individual responsibility and judgment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r1.claim: Then places belonging to the believers above the previously mentioned works in rank, implying that crossing the pass follows prior faith; the rebuked person lacked faith, without which good deeds bring no reward, so faith is a condition for their recognition.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r2.claim: Asked whether Ibn Judʿān benefited from pre-Islamic acts of kinship, feeding, freeing captives and slaves, and generosity for God's sake, the Prophet said no because he never asked forgiveness for his sin on Judgment Day.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r3.claim: The verse's implication is that such good deeds done before Islam would be praised if their performer later believed in God when Islam came.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p360/r4.claim: Those who take ثم temporally understand the sequence as crossing the pass in pre-Islamic life and adopting faith later; a sound report from Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām says the Prophet told him that Islam embraces past good deeds, and Ḥinath means worship.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r1.claim: Belonging to the community of believers indicates firmer, socially recognized faith than simply being called a believer; the group identity strengthens the praise.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r2.claim: The object of believed is omitted because it is understood as God alone, Muhammad as Messenger, and Islam; naming the believing group also leads naturally into praise of their patience and mercy and the promise of the people of the right.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r3.claim: Patience is the basis of good works because they require restraining desire, and mutual encouragement of mercy sustains the Muslim community; recommending mercy implies practicing it. The source links this to mutual mercy and feeding the poor.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p361/r4.claim: The praise indirectly rebukes idolaters as lacking patience and compassion, a contrast made explicit in the cited passages about calling to God, patience, honoring orphans, and feeding the needy.

TABATABAI:90:10-17/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:90:10-17/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:90:10-17/r9.claim: Mercy is a verbal noun: believers urge one another to patience in obedience to God and compassion toward the poor, needy, and destitute.

BINTSHATI:v1p185/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p185/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p185/r4.claim: The author rejects the need for allegorical explanations because the Qur’an itself answers its question by defining the obstacle through emancipation, feeding, faith, patience, and mercy.

BINTSHATI:v1p188/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r1.claim: The author takes thumma as real sequence: restoring dignity through emancipation and social justice through feeding are prerequisites for faith and its mutual exhortations.

BINTSHATI:v1p188/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads thumma as distance in virtue and rank, not time, since faith precedes and validates good works.

BINTSHATI:v1p188/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān proposes rank rather than temporal delay because faith must precede valid deeds, or that the phrase describes dying in faith, or merely delayed mention.

BINTSHATI:v1p188/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p188/r4.claim: The author rejects readings that detach faith from emancipation and feeding, arguing genuine faith requires resistance to tyranny, enslavement, and indifference to the poor.

BINTSHATI:v1p189/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p189/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p189/r1.claim: The order makes human dignity and social justice grounds of faith; a society that accepts human enslavement and starvation cannot sustain sincere faith.

BINTSHATI:v1p189/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p189/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p189/r2.claim: The conjunction waw links faith directly with mutual exhortation: sound faith brings patience in the struggle for good and merciful solidarity among people.

BINTSHATI:v1p189/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p189/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p189/r3.claim: The ideal community speaks against injustice, since God gave people tongues and lips so they would not remain silent about truth.

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17-20:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17-20:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17-20:kommentar/r1.claim: The probably secondary closing stanza adds afterlife destinies for the saved and damned, extending the original ethical demand into opposing group identities and reflecting conflict around Muhammad.

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17-20:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17-20:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17-20:kommentar/r2.claim: The added ending continues the rhyme of verses 11–16 and completes a chiastic 4+6+6+4 design by matching the opening stanza's length.

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17:anmerkung/r1.claim: Verse 90:17 resembles the likely secondary 103:3, which links faith and righteous deeds with mutual exhortation to truth and patience.

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:17:anmerkung/r2.claim: For the verb ʾāmana, the note points to 69:33.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p317/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p317/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p317/r5.claim: Verses 8–17 list eyes, speech, moral awareness, freeing slaves, feeding the poor, faith, patience, and compassion as capacities and deeds that should overcome greed and serve God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p326/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p326/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p326/r6.claim: Sensitive people who notice the downtrodden should do the stated virtuous deeds and also join believers who counsel patience and sympathy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p327/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p327/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p327/r1.claim: Failure to do the deeds and join the faithful reflects an obstacle to moral and spiritual growth that the person has not overcome.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p327/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p327/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p327/r2.claim: Patience accompanies sympathy because virtuous deeds oppose inner desire and feel like climbing a slope; ṣabr means perseverance and steadfastness needed for that effort.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r4.claim: The era's gravest human problems were slavery, poverty, and lack of mercy; remedies were freeing slaves, feeding orphans and the poor, and urging patience and compassion.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r5.claim: This summary of Islamic social ethics gives examples rather than an exhaustive or restrictive list of good works.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r6.claim: Because good deeds gain value together with faith, verse 17 also requires belief; this may mean believing in the usefulness and necessity of good deeds.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r7.speaker: Hakîm b. Hizâm
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r7.claim: Hakim asked whether his pre-Islamic charity, manumissions, and care for kin earned reward; the Prophet replied that after becoming Muslim he would receive the reward for all those good deeds.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p252/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p252/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p252/r2.claim: The parent-and-child oath also anticipates the ending: raising, protecting, and feeding children require patience and mercy.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r1.claim: Labad contributes to the surah's collective pattern: parents and offspring, paired faculties and paths, several ascent duties, believers advising one another, and disbelievers gathered in Hell; the plain word many would lose this effect.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p272/r5.claim: Thumma here cannot mean chronological delay, which would put belief after the good deeds of freeing and feeding; its connective force is explained in the continuation.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.claim: The surah's hardships call for patience: choosing either path, climbing the ascent, serving the enslaved, enduring famine, and caring for orphans and the destitute all demand perseverance.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r2.claim: Believers need patience to obey God and avoid sin; patience is a governing thread of the surah.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r3.claim: Mercy fits every sense of hill: the resident Prophet deserves mercy rather than abuse, and at the conquest he treated Quraysh with clemency, calling it the day of mercy and releasing them.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r4.claim: The parent-and-child bond is one of mercy and dutiful care.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r5.claim: The boastful spender needs mercy so he directs his wealth to the needy instead of wasting it uselessly; the enslaved person also needs compassion.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p275/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p275/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p275/r1.claim: Famine is a crucial time to spread mercy, and orphans and poor people are among those most in need of it; believers should enjoin mercy on one another.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p275/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p275/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p275/r2.claim: Repeating the verb and preposition with both patience and mercy stresses that each separately deserves mutual exhortation; repeating only the preposition is weaker, and simple coordination weaker still.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r1.claim: Patience comes first because the surah has already described human toil, the difficult ascent, and the two paths; mercy follows the subsequent duties of freeing and feeding.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r2.claim: Surat al-Asr first enjoins mutual counsel in truth because that surah treats loss generally; this surah addresses one part of truth, mercy and feeding.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r3.claim: Truth precedes patience in al-Asr because truth is primary and patience must be directed toward truth; holding to truth itself requires patience, while this surah orders patience first for contextual reasons.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r4.claim: The believers who trust, counsel patience and mercy, free slaves, and feed the needy are people of the right side, associated with goodness, blessing, happiness, and receiving their records in the right hand.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p278/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p278/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p278/r1.claim: The words for famine, kinship, destitution, mercy, and the right and left groups share the pattern maf'alah, matching action, description, and reward.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p284/r6.claim: The surah is woven around five threads: human toil, breadth of meaning, collective action, patience, and mercy.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p385/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p385/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p385/r4.claim: Surah al-Fajr contrasts rich and poor, while al-Balad portrays expenditure and poverty; al-Fajr condemns neglect of orphans and the poor, and al-Balad commands feeding them.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p389/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p389/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p389/r3.claim: Birth itself entails hardship, linking the oath to humanity's creation in hardship; raising children also requires patience and compassion, matching the surah's ending and the Prophet's struggle.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r3.claim: Freeing and feeding are acts of compassion, and their vulnerable recipients especially need patience, linking the obstacle's tasks to the surah's counsel of mercy.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r4.claim: Then can indicate order of mention rather than chronology: faith has a higher rank and is foundational, since no deed benefits a person in the afterlife without faith.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p403/r5.claim: Unlike the common pairing “believed and did righteous deeds,” this verse omits the latter because it has already listed freeing and feeding as righteous works.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p404/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p404/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p404/r1.claim: Repeating the verb in “they counsel one another in patience and they counsel one another in compassion” is stronger than repeating only the preposition or using conjunction alone, because each virtue matters independently.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p404/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p404/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p404/r3.claim: Marḥamah is broader and more encompassing than raḥmah, and the surah's many relationships call for compassion rather than harm.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p404/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p404/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p404/r4.claim: Patience comes first because the surah first details hardship and effort, then turns to compassion in feeding orphans and the poor.

STUDYQURAN:90:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:90:17/r1.claim: Good works in verses 13–16 must be grounded in belief, the necessary condition for their acceptance.

STUDYQURAN:90:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:17/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:90:17/r2.claim: Exhorting to patience means supporting religious practice through hardship and opposition; exhorting to compassion means urging mercy toward God's creatures.

STUDYQURAN:90:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:17/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:90:17/r3.claim: A hadith says the Merciful shows mercy to the merciful and urges mercy toward people on earth.
